decisions.decision: Rollback uses the same version-1 data file even though a 1.4.0 save strips due times, so operators must keep a copy containing the assigned dues and preserve subsequent ticket changes when upgrading again.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have expected assigned due times to survive writes by 1.4.0 automatically while operators continue working on the rolled-back release.

decisions.decision: Response times run in elapsed hours, including nights, weekends and holidays.
decisions.alternative: The help desk may have meant hours during its staffed schedule so the response clock pauses outside working hours.

decisions.decision: New tickets get their due time at creation even with DUE_TIMES off, and the flag controls whether the HTTP API exposes or uses that time.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have wanted tickets created while the feature is off to get their first due time during backfill under the policy chosen for activation.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:5–15 (R-1 assignment and toggle retention, R-2 exposure and R-3 off-mode behavior)

decisions.decision: Backfill uses each ticket’s currently stored priority.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have meant to use the priority the ticket had when it was created, looking it up in the audit history for tickets that were reprioritized.

decisions.decision: An invalid SLA hours setting is treated as a configuration error that names the variable and prevents startup under the service’s existing configuration convention.
decisions.alternative: Operators may have wanted the service to warn and start using the built-in hours for that priority.

decisions.decision: When status and priority are both supplied, an overdue ticket can match either filter, preserving the running service’s OR behavior.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have expected overdue tickets to match both supplied filters, as the API documentation describes for status and priority.

decisions.decision: The work is handed back locally with fixture-based release checks and rollout instructions, leaving production preparation and activation to operators.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have expected an operator-assisted rehearsal on a copy of production data before accepting the handoff.
decisions.where: record/01-intake.md:173 (delivery summary); record/04-spec.md:51 (verification scope and production authority); repo/docs/shiploop/environment.md:3–6,18–20

decisions.decision: Backfill writes due times without adding audit entries or outbox notifications or changing ticket update timestamps.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have wanted the initial due assignment on existing tickets recorded as a visible event in their history.

decisions.decision: The enabled HTTP API shows ISO-formatted due times on ticket responses, while the existing CLI output and weekly report contracts are preserved.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have intended operators to see due times in the human-readable CLI views too, while keeping the raw columns used by the weekly report intact.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:9–11 (R-2), 21–27 (R-5 and CLI contract); repo/README.md:60–76 (CLI and weekly report)

decisions.decision: The overdue list keeps the existing ticket ID order and cursor pagination.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have wanted the overdue view ordered by earliest due time so agents see the oldest missed deadlines first.
